opus.why: Beat sheet built from a detailed outline with clear constraints (beat count, runtime, where the hook and midpoint go). It's structural work, not final copy, and Sonnet at high effort handles it fully.

fable.why: Beat sheet with timing, hook, and midpoint constraints from an existing outline; structured creative work that Sonnet handles at full quality, but VO intent and pacing need real care, so high effort.

opus.why: The table includes final VO and on-screen text for a funny short, plus a punchline that loops back to the start. Comedic copy the audience reads is where a weaker model shows.

fable.why: 45-second short beat sheet with hook, three turns, and a looping punchline; near-final VO text in Russian is audience-facing, so high effort, but Sonnet matches Opus on this scale.

opus.why: Long-read outline that maps seven given claims onto sections. The inputs are clear and the reasoning is well scoped.

fable.why: Long-read outline with claim-to-section mapping and orphan-claim flagging; requires careful structural reasoning across two source files, well within Sonnet at high effort.

opus.why: Practical chapter structure for a lead-magnet guide. This is standard structuring work and needs no deep judgment.

fable.why: Chapter structure for a practical brand guide for non-marketers; needs brand judgment and audience fit but is structural, not final copy. Sonnet high suffices.

opus.why: Course design that needs a prerequisite chain, a capstone using all six modules, and a guess at where learners drop off. That's real teaching-design judgment, so it benefits from Opus.

fable.why: Course design with prerequisite chain, capstone integrating all modules, and drop-off analysis; multi-constraint reasoning that Sonnet at high effort handles without quality loss.

opus.why: Brandbook consistency audit. The contradictions are easy to spot, but choosing which version should win is brand judgment, where quality matters most.

fable.why: Enumerating contradictions in a short brand book and proposing which version wins; mostly explicit mismatches, but thoroughness and brand judgment on resolution favor Sonnet over Haiku.

opus.why: Careful cross-check of a short spec (enums, limits, units, field names) plus a single-source-of-truth proposal. It's detail work that Sonnet at high effort does reliably.

fable.why: Cross-section mismatch audit of a short spec with a proposed source of truth; explicit discrepancies to enumerate in a table, Sonnet medium is thorough enough.

opus.why: Small follow-up edit: reorder and merge sections of an existing outline and move the callback to the end.

fable.why: Follow-up edits to an existing outline: swap, merge, and strengthen the ending; mostly mechanical with one small creative rewrite, continuing a Sonnet-tier task.

opus.why: Eight-episode season arc with a through-line, a turn in each episode and cliffhangers between them. The narrative judgment on this creative structure benefits from Opus.

fable.why: Eight-episode season arc with a throughline, per-episode turn and cliffhanger; narrative-structure judgment matters, but Sonnet at high effort delivers this planning document at full quality.
